boards.title: Neighborhood Bulletin Board — Upcoming
boards.body:
City Council Meeting — Thursday 7:00 PM, City Hall
Food Drive — Saturday 9 AM-1 PM, Community Center
Community Cleanup — Sunday 10 AM, meet at the park
School Board Meeting — Tuesday 6:30 PM, Public School
Farmers Market — every Saturday, Main Street

boards.title: Public Transit Expansion Survey
boards.body: The city is asking riders to weigh in on new bus routes and stop frequency. Scan the code or visit City Hall to share your input.

boards.title: Learn How Local Government Works
boards.body: Free weekly sessions at the library explain how the council, county, and school board fit together — no registration needed, drop in any Wednesday evening.

boards.title: Neighborhood Planning Workshop
boards.body: Residents are invited to help sketch ideas for the vacant lot on 5th Street. All ages welcome — materials and coffee provided.

boards.title: Register to Vote
boards.body: Registration deadlines, sample ballots, and polling locations for the upcoming election. City Hall staff can help you check your registration status.

boards.title: Coffee Shop
boards.body: Locally owned, always busy before the morning commute. A regular meeting spot for neighbors catching up.

boards.title: Grocery Store
boards.body: A mid-size independent grocer — one of the few in walking distance for the apartment residents nearby.

boards.title: Pharmacy
boards.body: Handles prescriptions for most of the neighborhood; also a flu-shot clinic site every fall.

boards.title: Barber Shop
boards.body: Three chairs, no appointments needed most days. An informal hub for neighborhood conversation.

boards.title: Laundromat
boards.body: Open late, mostly serves renters in the apartment complex without in-unit laundry.

boards.title: Restaurant
boards.body: Family-run for over a decade. Business slows during road construction and picks back up for festivals.

boards.title: Bookstore
boards.body: Small independent shop that hosts the after-school reading group on Wednesdays.

boards.title: Bakery
boards.body: Opens at 5 AM. Supplies bread to two of the restaurants on this block.

boards.title: Flower Shop
boards.body: Sources some stock from the community garden's surplus program.

boards.title: Public Library
boards.body: Also runs the after-school program and hosts community meetings when City Hall's rooms are booked.

boards.title: Police Station
boards.body: Community policing office — also coordinates the neighborhood watch program.

boards.title: Fire Department
boards.body: Covers this district plus two neighboring ones; funded through the city's public safety budget.

boards.title: Community Center
boards.body: Hosts the food drive, youth programs, and rentable rooms for resident group meetings.

boards.title: Public School
boards.body: K-8 school; the School Board (a separate elected body from City Council) oversees its budget.

boards.title: Health Clinic
boards.body: A city-subsidized clinic offering low-cost care, partly funded through the public health budget line.

boards.title: Transit Station
boards.body: The regional bus line's main stop for this district — proposed for expanded service pending council review.

boards.title: Join the Off-Season Canvass
boards.body: Elections aren't the only reason to knock on doors. Our volunteer canvassers check in with neighbors year-round about road repairs, park upkeep, and city services — no campaign required. Sign up at the Community Engagement Office in City Hall.
